description: Facts about the CURRENT design/implementation that the Health v2 contract records. Each entry is asserted by the golden test, so a change to existing code, registry, package or docs that alters one of them fails the test and forces the contract to be revisited. Nothing here changes behaviour.

mismatches.statement: docs/SYSTEM_HEALTH_ARCHITECTURE.md still says 'The full 43-check architecture' and '17 of 46 reason codes'; the registry has 63 checks and 70 reason codes.

Home Assistant implements ten per-subsystem sensors only. The rollup sensor.ecco_system_health, the attention flag and a gating manual-control-ready entity do not exist; the one readiness entity is labelled REFERENCE ONLY, DO NOT USE TO GATE.
The engine result types lack the evidence fields the architecture document lists (last_good, source_signals, age_seconds and the three subsystem flags on SubsystemResult).
evaluate_all does not treat an absent check as UNKNOWN in the overall rollup: overall can read HEALTHY while a required check is missing (readiness correctly fails closed).
A freshness timestamp in the future yields a negative age and HEALTHY; ecco_core.freshness treats a future observation time as never fresh.

Datetime subtraction between two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo ignores the UTC offset. With Europe/London local datetimes this gives wrong ages on the 25 h (25 Oct 2026) and 23 h (28 Mar 2027) nights. UTC-aware inputs, or different tzinfo objects, are correct.
OverallHealthResult.severity_rank is the tier-capped rank, so UNKNOWN from an INFORMATIONAL subsystem reports state UNKNOWN with rank 1 while SEVERITY_RANK[UNKNOWN] is 2.

The HA communications row evaluates the two online flags only (no 60/180/600 s brackets) and maps any state other than 'on', including unknown and unavailable, to FAILED; the engine separates UNKNOWN from FAILED.
rtc_stall_detected is a plain boolean check: an isolated and a sustained stall give the same WARNING; there is no duration input.

With automatic clock sync OFF, rtc_drift_uncorrected is SUPPRESSED with no reason code; overall stays HEALTHY and control stays ready; no registry reason code names 'sync disabled'; HA does not represent rtc_drift_uncorrected.

failure_counter_delta needs a baseline at least window_seconds old (otherwise UNKNOWN) and reports UNKNOWN after a reset; the HA RTC row, per its documentation, latches WARNING for 1800 s after an observed increase and treats a reset as baseline-only. HA templates were not evaluated in this job.
HA transaction durations are derived from last_changed and under-report across a Home Assistant restart or ESPHome reconnect (documented limitation).
The reason an UNKNOWN was produced exists only as free human_reason text; there is no machine-readable subtype.

Freshness limits live in three places: registry warning and failure thresholds, the ecco_core.freshness catalogue (failure threshold only; the 60/180 s warning tiers appear only in a note), and HA templates (none). Registry failure thresholds and the catalogue agree today for telemetry (180 s) and configuration (600 s).
